source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Memento stores each case as a (state=task, action=plan, reward=success flag) triple, with failed runs kept. Retrieval by similarity or a learned Q-value. Case memory adds a small but steady gain on top of planning.
numbers: DeepResearcher avg F1/PM: planner without CBR 59.9/72.2 vs with CBR 66.6/80.4 (about +6.7/+8.2). Ablation: CBR +3.7 F1 / +5.3 PM on SimpleQA; +4.5/+7.0 on HLE. GAIA val 87.88 Pass@3 (GPT-4.1 planner, o3 executor); test 79.40.
limits: Authors' own numbers. Test score from a leaderboard. Gain from planning is larger than gain from cases.
agent_relevance: Supports the S9 record being a triple of problem, plan and outcome flag, including failures. The case effect is real but secondary to the loop around it.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: More retrieved cases barely help. Going from zero cases to one gives almost the whole gain. Four is about the best.
limits: One planner/executor pair (gpt-4.1 / o4-mini). Single run per cell, no error bars.
agent_relevance: Retrieve few cases (1 to 4) at S1/S2. Flooding the prompt with records gives no extra value.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Learning curve with and without case memory is almost the same by the fifth pass. The no-CBR system also climbs, so most of the climb is not due to cases.
numbers: Table 4 (DeepResearcher): no CBR 78.65, 80.93, 82.62, 83.53, 84.47 over iterations 1-5; non-parametric CBR 79.84, 81.87, 83.09, 84.03, 84.85; parametric CBR 80.46, 82.84, 84.10, 84.85, 85.44. Gap at iteration 5: +0.4 (non-param), +1.0 (param).
limits: The no-CBR arm also rises about 5.8 points; the paper does not explain why. No significance test.
agent_relevance: Warning: report case-memory gains against a control that gets the same repeated runs. A rise over time is not proof the records helped.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Out-of-distribution test: cases from four training sets were stored, four retrieved per query on three unseen sets.
numbers: Absolute gains 4.7 to 9.6 points. Ablation table (F1/PM) Memento vs Memento w/o CBR: Musique 40.6/53.3 vs 35.6/43.8; Bamboogle 86.2/92.8 vs 77.5/83.2; PopQA 64.0/72.5 vs 57.9/63.9.
limits: Case bank from about 3k training questions. Authors say the bank saturates quickly and a small curated memory is best.
agent_relevance: Cases transfer across question styles when the stored plan is generic; supports storing plans, not answers.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: AWM stores abstract workflows (sub-routines with example-specific values replaced by placeholders) instead of full trajectories. Big gains on WebArena.
numbers: WebArena total success: BrowserGym baseline 23.5 vs AWM 35.5 (+12.0 absolute, +51.1% relative), gpt-4, 812 tasks; about 2.0 fewer steps per task. Beat a method using human-written workflows (32.0) by 7.6% relative.
limits: Online setting, no train split. GPT-4 temperature 0. Single run.
agent_relevance: Evidence that the S9 lesson should be abstracted (placeholders for names and values), not a raw transcript.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Direct test of abstract workflows vs concrete full-trajectory exemplars (Synapse) on Mind2Web cross-task.
numbers: AWM (gpt-3.5) element accuracy 39.0 vs Synapse 34.0 (+5.0); step SR 34.6 vs 30.6 (+4.0). With gpt-4: AWM 50.6 elem acc, 45.1 step SR, 4.8 task SR vs MindAct-4 41.6, 36.2, 2.0.
limits: Retrieval and prompting differ between systems; the explanation (concrete examples bias element choice) is not isolated by a controlled experiment.
agent_relevance: Competing explanation: abstract records avoid copying surface details. Test abstraction vs raw record in our own S9.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Offline vs online workflow induction: induced workflows come from model-predicted trajectories that may be wrong. Online wins when the test domain differs from training.
numbers: Margin of online over offline grows 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test gap widens (abstract). Cross-task element accuracy offline 50.6 vs online 50.0; cross-domain online 40.9 vs offline 36.4.
limits: Authors admit induced workflows can be incorrect and degrade performance. Quality checked on a small sample.
agent_relevance: Own-run records beat imported ones when classes shift. Gate what is stored by a checked outcome (G2/G3).

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: ExpeL keeps two kinds of memory: raw successful trajectories (retrieved by task similarity) and distilled natural-language insights from success/failure pairs. Both parts matter; which matters more depends on the task.
numbers: Insights-only vs retrieval-only success: HotpotQA 36% vs 31%; ALFWorld 50% vs 55%; WebShop 37% vs 38%. Full ExpeL beat ReAct on all three. ALFWorld: ReAct 40%, ExpeL 59% (one attempt).
limits: Small benchmarks, gpt-3.5 actor, gpt-4 insight extractor; few seeds.
agent_relevance: Our record should hold both a concrete case and a short distilled rule, kept separate.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Ablations on what to store and how to retrieve. Retrieval by task similarity beats retrieval by reasoning-step similarity and beats random. Learned insights beat hand-written ones. Adding reflections to the insight prompt hurt.
numbers: ALFWorld SR: ReAct 40.0, reasoning-similarity 48.5, random 42.5, task-similarity (ExpeL) 59.0. HotpotQA SR: ReAct 28.0, hand-crafted insights 32.0, insights with reflections 29.0, gpt-3.5-written insights 32.0, ExpeL 39.0.
limits: Insight quality depends on the extractor model. Random examples are barely above no memory.
agent_relevance: Index cases by the problem statement (task similarity), not by the agent's inner reasoning. Use the strongest model for the lesson line.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Failure/success pairs are the raw material for good insights. Insights extracted only from the few-shot examples gave no gain over ReAct. Experience gathered with retries beat experience from single attempts.
numbers: Few-shot-only insights: no advantage over ReAct (Fig. 6). Transfer HotpotQA to FEVER: Act 58, ReAct 63, ExpeL transfer without demos 65, with demos 70 (SR %). ALFWorld with Reflexion rounds: ExpeL R0 59.0 to R3 64.2.
limits: Transfer is one source/target pair.
agent_relevance: Record the failing attempt next to the passing one; a lesson line needs both to be useful.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Reflexion stores a short first-person reflection after a failed trial instead of the whole trajectory. Reflection beat just keeping the last trajectory as memory.
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct+Reflexion solved 130 of 134 tasks. HotpotQA ablation: self-reflection gave an 8% absolute boost over episodic-memory-only (most recent trajectory). HumanEval Python pass@1 91.0 vs GPT-4 baseline 80.1. Rust ablation (50 hardest): without the self-reflection step no gain over baseline; without test generation 52% vs 60%.
limits: Gains rely on a real signal (tests, exact match, heuristics). Authors note flaky tests give false positives. Per-task memory only, not cross-task.
agent_relevance: Supports a one-line lesson written from real failing output (G2). Without a real check, reflection does not help.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
finding: Storing the agent's own successful trajectories (success only) and retrieving the top-k as examples raised success on three benchmarks. Gains equal or exceed a model upgrade.
numbers: gpt-4o-mini: ALFWorld 0.73 to 0.89; InterCode-SQL 0.75 to 0.79; Wordcraft 0.55 to 0.64. After 3500 training tasks ALFWorld +20 points over fixed DB vs +15 from upgrading to gpt-4o. With curation: ALFWorld 0.93, SQL 0.82, Wordcraft 0.69-0.72. Equal to pass@4 or pass@5 of the baseline.
limits: Success-only storage by design. Five trials per setting; benchmarks are repetitive task families. Fine-tuning on the same data did a bit better on ALFWorld (0.96 vs 0.93).
agent_relevance: Strong support for a case bank of own passed runs. Gain depends on task classes recurring.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
finding: Which cases to keep matters. Plain accumulation has high run-to-run variance. Keeping the best trajectory per task (by empirical utility as an example) beats keeping the worst.
numbers: Database-level curation (population of 5, bottom 20% replaced by top 20%) lifts ALFWorld 0.89 to 0.91 but not Wordcraft. Exemplar-level curation: SQL 0.79 to 0.81, Wordcraft 0.64 to 0.72. Best-vs-worst per-task selection separates curves on ALFWorld and Wordcraft.
limits: Curation effects of 1 to 8 points sit close to standard errors of 0.01 to 0.03; Wordcraft DB-curation gave no gain.
agent_relevance: Keep a per-record usefulness count in S9 (did using this record help?) and drop records that did not.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Agents copy retrieved cases. When the new problem is close to a stored one, the output is close to the stored output. So a wrong stored case is reproduced.
numbers: Pearson r near 1 between input similarity and output similarity for RegAgent with growing memory; four agents tested (RegAgent, EHRAgent, AgentDriver, CIC-IoT Agent).
quote: high similarity between a task input and the input in a retrieved memory record often results in highly similar agent outputs
limits: Specific task agents, not general reasoning. Exact table values were not recoverable from the text extraction.
agent_relevance: Our S9 records must be verified before reuse; a copied wrong record repeats the error (G3).

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Adding every run to memory is worse than a frozen small memory when the quality filter is weak. A strict (human oracle) filter keeps improving. A model judge can do more harm than a small hand-made set.
numbers: Add-all and coarse automatic evaluators gave flat or declining success curves; strict selective addition and a judge fine-tuned on only 300 trajectories kept improving. Error-propagation test: replacing agent output with ground truth in stored records widens the gap over time for add-all and coarse filters.
limits: Numeric table not recoverable from the text extract; four agents and several LLM backbones.
agent_relevance: Do not log lessons from unverified runs. Verification before storage is the main lever.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Deleting stored records that led to poor later results improved performance when the evaluator was reliable, and cut memory size. Some records that passed the filter still misled (misaligned replay).
numbers: History-based deletion beat periodic deletion with a strict evaluator; with a noisy evaluator it was unreliable and depended on the judge model. Periodic deletion cut memory a lot with small loss. Fixed capacity (100 records EHRAgent, 180 AgentDriver) with combined deletion beat fixed memory.
limits: Needs a trustworthy outcome label for each later use. Distribution shift test showed small gaps.
agent_relevance: Future outcomes are free labels for old records: track hit/miss per record and prune.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control
finding: Complete trajectories as exemplars, with state abstraction and a vector memory. Each part adds a little; memory adds least on Mind2Web.
numbers: MiniWoB++ mean success 99.2% (gpt-3.5-turbo, 50 episodes per task); RCI got 20%, 88%, 58% on guess-number, use-spinner, use-autocomplete vs Synapse 100%, 100%, 98%. Mind2Web cross-task step SR (gpt-3.5): MindAct 17.4, +state abstraction 25.2, +trajectory-as-exemplar 29.2, +memory 30.6; task SR 0.8, 2.0, 2.0, 2.4.
limits: Mind2Web task success stays very low (2.4% best). Memory gain of 1.4 step-SR points is small. Observation abstraction is a confound.
agent_relevance: Shrinking the stored observation (abstraction) mattered more than adding retrieval; store compact state descriptions.

source: Zeng et al. (2024) On the Structural Memory of LLM Agents
finding: Compared chunks, triples, atomic facts, summaries and a mix, across six datasets and three retrieval methods. No single format wins; the mix is best on average and most robust to noise.
numbers: Iterative retrieval, mixed memory: HotpotQA F1 82.11%, 2Wiki F1 68.15%. Triples 62.06% F1 on 2Wiki; atomic facts 81.29% on HotpotQA; chunks 31.63% F1 on NarrativeQA and 78.5% accuracy on QuALITY (reranking); summaries 32.26% F1 on NarrativeQA. Noise documents lower all formats; mix stays highest on HotpotQA. K=200 retrieved items hurt summaries.
limits: Document QA with gpt-4o-mini, not agent experience records. Single run.
agent_relevance: Argues for storing one record in more than one form (raw case plus short rule plus tags), not a single format.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: A curated, short memory beats appending the full history. Appending everything barely helps and can hurt.
numbers: AIME 2024 (30 problems): Claude 3.5 Sonnet baseline 23.3, full-history 26.7, DC-Cumulative 50.0; GPT-4o baseline 20.0, full-history 13.3, DC-RS 40.0. AIME 2025: Sonnet 6.7 / 6.7 / 36.7; GPT-4o 6.7 / 3.3 / 20.0. GPQA-Diamond Sonnet 59.6 to 68.7 (retrieval alone 63.6). Game of 24 GPT-4o 10% to 99% (empty-memory control 19%).
limits: Tiny test sets (30 problems for AIME). Game of 24 gain came from reusing one Python solution.
agent_relevance: Curate and compress; do not log transcripts. Big gains came from storing a reusable tool or snippet, not advice.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: Gains depend on the model. A weaker model gains less; a stronger one may not use the stored method.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Haiku AIME 2024 10.0 to 36.7 with DC-Cumulative; AIME 2025 only to 13.3. Claude 3.5 Sonnet on Game of 24 only 12% to 14%.
limits: Per-model, single runs, 30 items.
agent_relevance: Test the record format on the target model; do not assume transfer across models.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank
finding: ReasoningBank stores structured memory items: title, one-sentence description, 1-3 sentence content. Items are distilled from successes AND failures, judged by the agent itself.
numbers: WebArena overall success (Gemini-2.5-flash): no memory 40.5, Synapse 42.1, AWM 44.1, ReasoningBank 48.8, with test-time scaling 51.8. Overall gains over no memory +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 across three backbones.
limits: Authors' own comparison. Baselines re-implemented. At most 3 items per trajectory.
agent_relevance: Most direct template for the S9 lesson record: title, trigger description, short content. Keep it to a few sentences.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank
finding: Failures help only if the memory is built to use them. Methods that store successes only gain little or lose when failures are added.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash: Synapse 40.6 (success only) to 41.7 (with failures); AWM 44.4 to 42.2; ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7.
limits: One subset, one backbone.
agent_relevance: Store failures as a lesson (what to avoid and why), not as a trajectory to imitate.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank
finding: The judge that labels past runs can be wrong without ruining the gain, within limits.
numbers: Judge accuracy of 70% to 90% gave similar success rates; 100% (ground truth) was best. Without memory best-of-N rose only 39.0 to 42.2. Cross-site (Multi) subset: AWM gave no gain and degraded; ReasoningBank +4.6 over the strongest baseline.
limits: Self-judging in web tasks with usable page cues; code tasks have real tests.
agent_relevance: If we label with code checks, not self-judgment, the label problem is smaller. Abstracted items transfer better than workflows across sites.

source: Tang et al. (2025) Agent KB: Leveraging Cross-Domain Experience for Agentic Problem Solving
finding: Experience unit = task embedding, goal-constraint predicates, action-reasoning pairs, metadata. Adapting retrieved items before use matters; replaying a raw workflow gives less.
numbers: GAIA (smolagents, GPT-4.1) pass@1 55.15 to 61.21 with Agent KB; raw workflow instead of abstracted unit 58.18; removing the Refine step 55.15 (no gain, the largest drop, -6.06); removing Reason or Retrieve 60.00 / 57.58. pass@3 55.2 to 73.9. Level 3 stays 34.62 in most arms.
limits: Authors' benchmark, GAIA 165 tasks, few seeds. Human-curated 10 to 15 few-shot exemplars per domain build the abstraction.
agent_relevance: Retrieved cases must be adapted to the new problem, not pasted.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with LLMs
finding: Stores high-level thought templates (not cases) with a category and description, retrieved by embedding similarity of a distilled problem statement.
numbers: With GPT-4: +79.4% accuracy on Game of 24 vs GPT-4 baseline; +8.4% vs Tree of Thoughts; vs Meta-prompting +23% Game of 24, +20% Geometric Shapes, +51% Checkmate-in-One. Meta-buffer has 6 categories.
limits: Authors' own results; they state limits for creative problems and for templates built by a weaker model.
agent_relevance: A template per problem class is a cheaper alternative to a case bank; template quality depends on the writer model.

source: Wei et al. (2025) Evo-Memory: Benchmarking LLM Agent Test-time Learning with Self-Evolving Memory
finding: Benchmark of over ten memory modules on streaming tasks. A plain retrieve-and-condition baseline (ExpRAG) with entries (input, output, feedback) is strong and often beats complex designs. Gains track how similar the tasks are.
numbers: ReMem single-turn 0.65 average exact match; BabyAI 0.92/0.96, ScienceWorld 0.95/0.62 (Gemini/Claude). Gain vs within-dataset task similarity Pearson 0.717 (Gemini 2.5 Flash) and 0.563 (Claude 3.7 Sonnet). ALFWorld steps cut from 22.6 to 11.5. With unfiltered failures stored, baselines degrade notably.
quote: ExpRAG serves as a simple yet highly effective baseline
limits: Same authors propose ReMem. Task-similarity measure is cluster spread of embeddings. Modest gains on mixed sets (AIME-25, GPQA).
agent_relevance: Expect little gain from the case bank on diverse hard problems; it pays when classes recur. Keep entry = input, output, feedback.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG: Case-Based Reasoning for RAG in LLMs for Legal QA
finding: Case = (question, answer, support text, extracted entities) with dual embeddings. Hybrid matching beats single-field matching; including the full case in the prompt beats support text only.
numbers: Best: hybrid AnglEBERT with k=3 full cases; average gain 1.94% in semantic similarity over No-RAG; significant at 95% (ANOVA, paired tests) vs No-RAG and hybrid LegalBERT k=3. All hybrid variants beat No-RAG.
limits: Synthetic QA generated from the Australian Open Legal Corpus; no expert rating; cosine similarity as the metric; small gain.
agent_relevance: Which fields are indexed (problem text and solution support) changes retrieval; the general embedding beat the legal one here, so measure rather than assume.
